description: key-hierarchy design §5.6 (single writer): trees of epochs whose signatures verified (labels stand for their UTF-8 bytes; signer, reason, home after the epoch, list, recovery fingerprint, and for a takeover whether its recoverySig verified under the parent's recovery key), the device's pinned chain, and the expected chain, the pinned epochs a takeover dropped, the ignored epochs and the home conflicts. A takeover signed by its parent's kit but refused only because that kit was introduced below the pinned frontier is "deferred" (round 9, L3), not ignored; absent means none.

cases.name: home-signed epochs are followed linearly; a handoff moves home
a stolen home writing after the takeover's parent: the takeover wins, the stolen epochs are dropped
a stolen home writing after the takeover's parent: a joiner takes the takeover
a takeover on top of the stolen home's epochs keeps them as history; the stolen home is off every later list
two takeovers that are not ancestors of each other: the smaller epochId wins, silently
two takeovers: the device that made the larger one switches
a takeover below a takeover: followed, it is on the winner's chain
after a handoff the old home signing is ignored
an epoch signed by a listed device that is not home is ignored
a takeover without the recovery key's signature is ignored
a removed former home signing under an epoch where it was home: the pinned chain holds; a home conflict is reported
the same tree for a joiner: it stops at the conflict
at a home conflict the user picks the branch (round 7, M2)
a takeover settles the conflict for everyone
a stale device pinned on a home epoch the takeover did not see switches to it
a device pinned before the takeover follows it
a takeover may re-admit a device of an ancestor list that the stolen home removed
a takeover listing a device of no ancestor list is ignored
a takeover signed by a recovery key other than the parent's is ignored
round 7 C1: an old kit's takeover from before the replacement is refused by a device that saw the replacement
round 7 C1: the new kit's takeover is followed
round 7 C1 residual: a device pinned before the replacement still takes the old kit's takeover
round 7 C1 residual: a joiner that saw nothing takes it too
round 7 residual: a stolen home replaced the kit first; a device that saw it refuses the old-kit takeover
round 7: a device pinned before the stolen home's replacement takes the owner's takeover
round 8 C1-b: a device pinned before the stolen home's replacement takes the owner's takeover, not the thief's under its new kit
round 8 C1-b: a device that saw the replacement takes the thief's takeover (stated residual)
round 8 C1-b: a joiner picks by id (stated residual)
round 8 C1-b probe: pinned before the thief's replacement, the owner's takeover beats the thief's ground id
round 8 C1-b probe: a device that pinned the thief's replacement takes the thief's takeover (stated residual)
round 8 C1-b probe: a joiner picks by id (stated residual)
round 8 C1-b probe: without the thief's takeover the owner's wins
round 8 C1-b: a new kit's takeover waits one run on a device pinned before the replacement
round 8 C1-b: ... and is followed once the replacement is pinned
round 8 L1: a takeover listing a retired kit is ignored
